fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents strongly present the genuine Python, large-scale API, fleet-telematics, Kubernetes and observability fit. They appropriately acknowledge reduced recent coding in the CV and explain the return to individual-contributor work in the letter. They do not invent Docker, CI/CD, REST consumption, query tuning, safe schema migrations, EKS or EDI experience. However, several must-have areas remain unproven, and the limited, historical AWS exposure and current Go rustiness are not made explicit.

issues: The 'SELECTED ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE' heading is stranded at the foot of page one, with its content on page two.
Page one is dense while page two is only 29.7% filled.
The senior/staff target headline is reasonable, but the application could more clearly reassure the employer about acceptance of its role level and compensation.
FastAPI appears in the skills list, but naming it in the supported service-template achievement would provide stronger experience-level evidence.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in sensible order with intact words and standard headings.
Strong direct matches include Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform and all three observability tools.
Several explicit must-have screening terms are absent, notably Docker, REST and CI/CD.
The missing query-tuning, migration, Docker and CI/CD claims cannot safely be added from the supplied material.
Event-ingestion and transport coverage is semantic, through GPS ingestion, fleet telematics and route history, rather than exact keyword repetition.

issues: The third paragraph is a dense skills catalogue rather than a sharply selected example.
Successive sentences begin 'I have also' and 'I also bring', creating avoidable repetition.
The letter does not explicitly reassure the employer that a lower salary and a non-director title are acceptable.
It could connect the fleet-ingestion and Kafka experience more specifically to Tessel's carrier-event pipeline and announced Kafka transition.
It explains the career change but does not include the CV's useful qualification that recent coding has mainly involved internal tools.
strengths: Names Tessel Cargo Software and the Backend Engineer (Python) role correctly.
Clearly explains the intentional return from management to hands-on individual-contributor work.
Uses substantiated throughput and availability achievements.
Makes a credible connection between fleet telematics and shipment tracking.
References company-specific engineering practices: ownership, concise design notes and sustainable reliability.
Avoids carrying over the earlier letter's internal-promotion context or outdated Principal Engineer framing.

spacing_issues: The CV's 'SELECTED ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE' heading is orphaned at the bottom of page one.
Its blue section rule appears at the top of page two, separated from the heading.
The CV has an unbalanced page distribution: a densely packed first page and a second page only 29.7% filled.
The skills line breaks 'AWS (EC2, S3)' so that 'S3)' sits alone on the following line.
consistency_issues: The CV uses blue section rules and a large name header, whereas the letter is plain; the shared serif typography still makes them reasonably compatible.
The additional-experience date is embedded in its bold title line rather than following the right-aligned date treatment used for employment.
issues: The automated measurements report no problems, but the page images clearly reveal the orphaned heading and split section rule.
The two-page length is justified by seniority; the problem is pagination and balance rather than page count.
The cover letter is clean and readable, with normal whitespace below the signature.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “I have also worked with Kubernetes ... I also bring practical automated-testing experience” repeats the same transition in adjacent sentences.

“PostgreSQL/PostGIS and message-oriented systems, Kafka, and production observability” is an awkwardly coordinated list; grouping databases, messaging and observability separately would read more naturally.

notes_facts_used: The letter uses the genuine desire to return to hands-on individual-contributor work.
The CV uses the senior/staff backend target level.
The CV explicitly states that recent coding has focused on internal tools and Python cost-dashboard scripts.
notes_facts_ignored: Explicit willingness to accept lower compensation and a senior-engineer title.
Limited and historical AWS exposure, with GCP as the main cloud.
The reorganisation explanation for departure and availability of a reference.

parsed.summary: Both documents are factually well grounded and successfully reposition an experienced engineering director for hands-on backend work without inventing missing qualifications. The strongest evidence is the high-throughput API work, Python service migration, fleet-telematics ingestion and observability experience. Important requirements remain only partly demonstrated, particularly Docker, CI/CD, REST consumption, query tuning and schema migrations, while limited AWS depth and acceptance of the lower role level could be communicated more clearly. The main presentation defect is the CV's orphaned section heading and unbalanced pagination; the cover letter is readable, relevant and free of stale framing.
